items.readable_text:
Content:
To negate a statement with nested quantifiers, we apply the formulas for negating a quantifier several times, from left to right.

Content:
For example, let's negate the following (true) statement:

Content:
[MATH: \forall x \in \mathbb{N}, \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x < y]

Content:
First, we negate the external quantifier [MATH: \forall{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ¬(∀x ∈ N, ∃y ∈ R, x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ¬(∃y ∈ R, x < y)]

Content:
Next, we negate the internal quantifier [MATH: \exists{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ∃x ∈ N, ¬(∃y ∈ R, x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, ¬(x < y)]

Content:
Finally, we negate the underlying predicate:

Content:
[MATH: ∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, ¬(x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, x ≥ y]

Content:
In short, we flip all the quantifiers and negate the predicate.

sections.normalized_html: Consider the following statement: [MATH: \exists x \in X, \, \exists y \in Y, \, P(x,y) \Rightarrow Q(x,y)] What is the negation of this statement?
sections.readable_text:
Consider the following statement:
[MATH: \exists x \in X, \, \exists y \in Y, \, P(x,y) \Rightarrow Q(x,y)]
What is the negation of this statement?

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall that [MATH: P(x,y) \Rightarrow Q(x,y)\equiv \neg P(x,y) \lor Q(x,y).]

So, our statement now reads

[MATH: \exists x \in X, \, \exists y \in Y, \, \neg P(x,y) \lor Q(x,y).]

To negate this statement, we flip the quantifiers and negate the predicate:

[MATH: ¬(∃x ∈ X, ∃y ∈ Y, ¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))|≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))]

Finally, by applying De Morgan's law for disjunctions, we have the following:

[MATH: ∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))|≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y))∧¬Q(x, y); ≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, P(x, y)∧¬Q(x, y)]

items.title: Negating Statements Involving Nested Quantifiers

sections.normalized_html:
Negate the following quantified statement:

[MATH: \qquad] There exists a natural number [MATH: n] such that [MATH: x^n \geq 0] for any real number [MATH: x.]
sections.readable_text:
Negate the following quantified statement:

[MATH: \qquad] There exists a natural number [MATH: n] such that [MATH: x^n \geq 0] for any real number [MATH: x.]

sections.normalized_html:
The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

[MATH: \qquad] There exists [MATH: n \in \mathbb{N}] such that, for all [MATH: x \in \mathbb{R},] [MATH: x^n \geq 0.]

Writing this symbolically, we have:

[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: \exists n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \, x^n \geq 0]

To negate a quantified statement, we flip the quantifiers and negate the predicate: [MATH: ¬(∃n ∈ N, ∀x ∈ R, x^{n} ≥ 0)|≡∀n ∈ N, ∃x ∈ R, ¬(x^{n} ≥ 0); ≡∀n ∈ N, ∃x ∈ R, x^{n} < 0]

which reads

[MATH: \qquad] For all [MATH: n \in \mathbb{N}] there exists [MATH: x \in \mathbb{R}] such that [MATH: x^n \lt 0,]

or simply

[MATH: \qquad] For any natural number [MATH: n] there exists a real number [MATH: x] such that [MATH: x^n \lt 0.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
To negate a statement with nested quantifiers, we apply the formulas for negating a quantifier several times, from left to right.

Content:
For example, let's negate the following (true) statement:

Content:
[MATH: \forall x \in \mathbb{N}, \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x < y]

Content:
First, we negate the external quantifier [MATH: \forall{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ¬(∀x ∈ N, ∃y ∈ R, x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ¬(∃y ∈ R, x < y)]

Content:
Next, we negate the internal quantifier [MATH: \exists{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ∃x ∈ N, ¬(∃y ∈ R, x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, ¬(x < y)]

Content:
Finally, we negate the underlying predicate:

Content:
[MATH: ∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, ¬(x < y)≡∃x ∈ N, ∀y ∈ R, x ≥ y]

Content:
In short, we flip all the quantifiers and negate the predicate.

---

Item 2 — Example: Negating Statements in Symbolic Form Containing a General Predicate

Example Prompt:
Consider the following statement:
[MATH: \exists x \in X, \, \exists y \in Y, \, P(x,y) \Rightarrow Q(x,y)]
What is the negation of this statement?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we recall that
[MATH: P(x,y) \Rightarrow Q(x,y)\equiv \neg P(x,y) \lor Q(x,y).]

So, our statement now reads

[MATH: \exists x \in X, \, \exists y \in Y, \, \neg P(x,y) \lor Q(x,y).]

To negate this statement, we flip the quantifiers and negate the predicate:

[MATH: ¬(∃x ∈ X, ∃y ∈ Y, ¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))|≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))]

Finally, by applying De Morgan's law for disjunctions, we have the following:

[MATH: ∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y)∨Q(x, y))|≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, ¬(¬P(x, y))∧¬Q(x, y); ≡∀x ∈ X, ∀y ∈ Y, P(x, y)∧¬Q(x, y)]
